title: [Bug] DSPARK silently corrupts identifiers on DeepSeek-V4-Flash, making speculative decoding unsafe
body:
### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug

Summary

On DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, SGLang’s DSPARK speculative decoding silently introduces single-character corruptions into identifiers supplied verbatim in the prompt:

kimi-k3   → kimi-kw
nova-x7   → nova-7
apollo-n9 → apollo-n11

The same server, weights, prompts, and launch configuration—with only speculative decoding disabled—produces zero such corruptions across thousands of grounded identifier tokens.

The corruption rate increases with the DSPARK verify-window width:

--speculative-dspark-block-size | speculative_num_draft_tokens | Temp 0 | Temp 1 -- | -- | -- | -- 6 | 7 | 1.03% | 0.82% 5 | 6 | 0.32% | 0.77% 1 | 2 | 0.00% | 0.00% Speculation disabled | — | 0.00% | 0.00%

Aggregated across both block_size=1 runs:

  • Temperature 0: 0 / 4561
  • Temperature 1: 0 / 3701

Using the rule of three, the corresponding approximate 95% upper bounds are:

  • Temperature 0: <0.066%
  • Temperature 1: <0.081%

This contrasts with the 1.03% observed rate at block_size=6, temperature 0.

Examples of corrupted identifiers

Malformed forms observed at block_size=6, temperature 0:

kimi-kw    -> kimi-k3   (x5)
kimi-k2    -> kimi-k3   (x3)
kimi-k7    -> kimi-k3   (x2)
apollo-n11 -> apollo-n9 (x2)
nova-12    -> nova-x7   (x2)
wq-7f2e    -> wq-7f2b   (x2)

kimi-kw2   -> kimi-k3
kimi-v2    -> kimi-k3
kimi-k11   -> kimi-k3
apollo-n12 -> apollo-n9
nova-7     -> nova-x7
nova-v7    -> nova-x7
wq-7f2e2   -> wq-7f2b

These are not malformed responses or obvious decoding failures. They are plausible-looking, single-character-wrong identifiers embedded in otherwise normal output.

Expected behavior

At temperature 0, DSPARK should emit the same greedy token sequence as the target model without speculative decoding.

A draft token should only be committed if it matches the corresponding target prediction. On mismatch, DSPARK should emit the target prediction instead.

Therefore, enabling DSPARK should not change grounded identifiers from:

kimi-k3

to:

kimi-kw

when the non-speculative target forward selects the correct token.

Actual behavior

With multi-position DSPARK verification enabled:

  • Grounded identifiers are silently corrupted.
  • The issue reproduces at temperature 0.
  • The issue requires or is strongly amplified by heterogeneous concurrent batching.
  • The rate increases with verify-window width.
  • No request error or warning is produced.
  • The finish reason remains normal.
  • Disabling speculation eliminates the corruption.
  • Reducing DSPARK to block_size=1 eliminates the corruption.

Hypotheses investigated and ruled out

1. Lossy accept/verify rule

This does not appear to be the cause.

Both accept_greedy and accept_greedy_triton in:

sglang/kernels/ops/speculative/dspark/dspark_accept.py

delegate to compute_dflash_correct_drafts_and_bonus in:

sglang/srt/speculative/dflash_utils.py

The relevant logic is:

matches = candidates[:, 1:] == target_predict[:, :-1]
correct_len = matches.to(torch.int32).cumprod(dim=1).sum(dim=1)
bonus = target_predict[torch.arange(bs, ...), correct_len]

Every committed token should therefore be either:

  1. An accepted draft token that compared equal to target_predict; or
  2. The bonus token, which is taken directly from target_predict.

A mismatching draft token should not be able to leak into the output.

This implies that the corrupted emitted tokens are likely themselves present in target_predict. In other words, the target verify forward appears to be producing incorrect logits or incorrect token alignment.

2. Ragged verify-window misalignment

accept_greedy performs:

torch.argmax(target_logits, dim=-1).view(
    bs, verify_num_draft_tokens
)

A dense reshape could misalign tokens if requests had different verify lengths.

However, SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE defaults to static. In static mode, resolve_ragged_verify_layout returns None, and verify lengths are uniform.

Therefore, the rectangular reshape is expected to be valid for this reproduction.

3. Numerical noise or batch-shape-dependent reductions

We tested three separate interventions. Each was verified to engage, and none removed the corruption.

FP32 LM head

Enabled:

--enable-fp32-lm-head

Engagement was confirmed empirically:

  • Before the change, 65.5% of recorded margins fell on the 0.25 BF16 grid.
  • After the change, 0% did.
  • There were zero exact ties across 34,420 records.

The typo rate did not improve.

Deterministic FP32 MoE reduction

We forced:

use_atomic_add = False

so the already-passed:

use_fp32_reduce = True

would engage.

In:

sglang/kernels/ops/moe/moe_wna16_marlin.py

the FP32 temporary buffer is allocated only under:

if use_fp32_reduce and not use_atomic_add:

This provides a structural confirmation that the path was active.

The observed rates remained approximately:

  • Temperature 0: 1.03%
  • Temperature 1: 0.82%

Tie epsilon on sampled accept path

Adding a tie epsilon to the sampled acceptance path had no effect.

More generally, an identifier repeated verbatim several times in the prompt should usually be a high-margin prediction. Low-order numerical noise would not be expected to repeatedly transform such identifiers into plausible alternatives.

The non-speculative control also varies in free-form prose between temperature-0 runs—likely due to prefix-cache or chunked-prefill effects—but it never corrupts a grounded identifier.

4. Draft/target gamma mismatch

The CLI can override the draft checkpoint’s declared gamma with only a warning:

DSpark gamma mismatch: using gamma=6
(from speculative_num_draft_tokens=7)
but draft config block_size=5.

This occurs in:

sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_config.py

The draft module itself obtains gamma from the checkpoint:

self.gamma = int(dspark_config.resolve_gamma(...))

in:

sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4_dspark.py

This means the draft module and worker may disagree about the verify-window width.

However, running with block_size=5:

  • Makes the configured values agree
  • Removes the warning
  • Still reproduces the bug

Observed rates at block_size=5 were:

  • Temperature 0: 0.32%
  • Temperature 1: 0.77%

Therefore, the gamma mismatch is not the root cause of this corruption, although the silent override may be worth hardening as a separate issue.

5. Draft-side kernels

SGLANG_DSPARK_FAST_KERNEL only gates the draft forward.

Under a correct speculative verification rule, draft quality may affect acceptance and performance, but it should not affect temperature-0 correctness. Incorrect draft tokens should be rejected in favor of the target prediction.

Therefore, a draft-only kernel failure does not explain committed token corruption unless there is also a target-verification or alignment bug.

Suspected fault area

The following is a hypothesis, not yet a verified root cause.

Given that:

  1. The accept rule appears to emit only target_predict;
  2. The corruption reproduces at temperature 0;
  3. The corruption disappears at a two-position verify window;
  4. The rate generally increases with verify-window width;
  5. Multiple numerical-determinism interventions had no effect; and
  6. The issue depends on concurrent heterogeneous batching,

the likely fault is in the target verify forward for multi-position DSPARK verification, especially for in-block positions t >= 1.

Potential areas include:

  • Intra-block causal masking
  • Position-ID construction or indexing
  • KV-cache placement for draft positions
  • Request-to-token mapping under heterogeneous batching
  • CUDA graph replay metadata for TARGET_VERIFY
  • Batch-slot reuse or stale per-request metadata
  • dsv4 attention behavior during multi-token verification

The current evidence suggests the target verification pass is computing incorrect logits or associating correct logits with the wrong request/position.

We have not yet isolated the specific kernel or metadata transition.

Suggested next diagnostics

A useful first datapoint would be:

--speculative-dspark-block-size 2

This would help distinguish between:

  • Failure beginning at the first genuinely multi-position verify step; and
  • Error probability accumulating with larger verify windows.

Other useful comparisons may include:

  1. DSPARK with CUDA graphs disabled.
  2. DSPARK with the hierarchical cache disabled.
  3. DSPARK with radix cache and chunked prefill disabled.
  4. An alternate attention backend, if DeepSeek-V4-Flash supports one.
  5. Capturing target_predict before acceptance and comparing it against independent one-token target forwards.
  6. Logging request IDs, verify positions, position IDs, and KV locations for the first divergent token.

Workaround

Both of the following avoid the observed corruption:

Option 1: Disable speculative decoding

This is the safest workaround.

Option 2: Use block_size=1

--speculative-algorithm DSPARK \
--speculative-dspark-block-size 1

This produced zero true typos across:

  • 4,561 grounded identifiers at temperature 0
  • 3,701 grounded identifiers at temperature 1

However, this sacrifices most of the speculative speedup, so it is a mitigation rather than a practical fix.

Until the multi-position verification issue is resolved, DSPARK should not be used with DeepSeek-V4-Flash for workloads where exact token reproduction matters.

Reproduction notes

DeepGEMM JIT warmup

Changing:

--speculative-dspark-block-size

changes num_tokens_per_req and invalidates the DeepGEMM JIT shape cache.

The first launch after changing this value may compile approximately 16,000 shapes and exceed a 3,600-second readiness budget. If the process is killed during warmup, it may look like an unrelated startup failure.

Please allow additional warmup time when changing the block size.

Log probabilities unavailable

DSPARK currently rejects:

"return_logprob": true

with:

DFLASH speculative decoding does not support return_logprob yet

Therefore, per-token target margins cannot currently be collected over HTTP on the affected speculative arm.

Severity

This is a silent data-corruption issue, not only a quality or performance regression.

The generated response is well-formed, and the corrupted identifier often looks plausible. Downstream systems therefore have no reliable way to distinguish the incorrect value from an intended value.

For DeepSeek-V4-Flash, this makes multi-position DSPARK speculative decoding unsafe for exact-identifier and tool-use workloads.

### Reproduction

Reproduction

The corruption usually requires concurrent, heterogeneous batching. A single request in isolation may not reproduce it. The script below sends four byte-identical target requests and four variable-length distractor requests per round.

1. Launch the affected DSPARK configuration

python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path <deepseek-v4-flash-0731> \
  --tp 4 \
  --attention-backend dsv4 \
  --moe-runner-backend marlin \
  --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \
  --speculative-dspark-block-size 6 \
  --max-running-requests 16 \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 16

2. Save the reproduction script

Save the following code as dspark_typo_repro.py:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Concurrency typo probe for one model and temperature."""

import collections
import concurrent.futures
import json
import os
import re
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request


MODEL = os.environ["TEST_MODEL"]
TEMP = float(os.environ.get("TEST_TEMP", "0"))
ROUNDS = int(os.environ.get("TEST_ROUNDS", "30"))
BASE = os.environ.get("TEST_BASE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:30000")
URL = f"{BASE}/v1/chat/completions"

IDS = [
    "kimi-k3",
    "nova-x7",
    "atlas-j9",
    "wq-7f2b",
    "zeta-r1",
    "apollo-n9",
]

CTX = " ".join(
    f"event{i}=ok latency={i % 37}ms owner=team{i % 9}"
    for i in range(350)
)

PROMPT = (
    f"Analyze this deployment history and write a 6-section operational report. "
    f"{CTX}\n"
    f"Canonical identifiers: {', '.join(IDS)}. "
    "Include a table and prose recap. "
    "Use every identifier at least four times, always verbatim; "
    "do not invent or normalize identifiers."
)

RX = re.compile(r"[a-z][a-z0-9]*-[a-z0-9]+", re.I)


def lev(a, b):
    prev = list(range(len(b) + 1))

    for i, x in enumerate(a, 1):
        cur = [i]

        for j, y in enumerate(b, 1):
            cur.append(
                min(
                    cur[-1] + 1,
                    prev[j] + 1,
                    prev[j - 1] + (x != y),
                )
            )

        prev = cur

    return prev[-1]


def ask(prompt=PROMPT, max_tokens=700, retries=5):
    body = json.dumps(
        {
            "model": MODEL,
            "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
            "max_tokens": max_tokens,
            "temperature": TEMP,
            "top_p": 1.0,
        }
    ).encode()

    for n in range(retries):
        request = urllib.request.Request(
            URL,
            data=body,
            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
        )

        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=300) as response:
                result = json.load(response)
                return result["choices"][0]["message"]["content"] or ""
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
            if error.code not in (429, 503) or n + 1 == retries:
                raise

            time.sleep(0.3 * (n + 1))

    raise RuntimeError("retries exhausted")


wrong = collections.Counter()
truncations = collections.Counter()
error_types = collections.Counter()

exact = 0
grounded = 0
responses = 0
errors = 0
typo_responses = 0
started = time.time()

with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=8) as pool:
    for rnd in range(ROUNDS):
        futures = [pool.submit(ask) for _ in range(4)]

        # Variable-length distractors perturb server-side batch composition.
        for j in range(4):
            length = 50 + ((rnd * 67 + j * 97) % 500)
            distractor = "Summarize: " + " ".join(
                f"word{k}" for k in range(length)
            )
            futures.append(pool.submit(ask, distractor, 128))

        for future in futures[:4]:
            try:
                text = future.result()
                responses += 1
            except Exception as error:
                errors += 1
                error_types[type(error).__name__] += 1
                continue

            response_has_typo = False

            for token in (
                match.lower().rstrip(".,;:")
                for match in RX.findall(text)
            ):
                if token in IDS:
                    exact += 1
                    grounded += 1
                    continue

                distance, target = min(
                    (lev(token, identifier), identifier)
                    for identifier in IDS
                )

                if distance <= 2:
                    grounded += 1

                    if any(identifier.startswith(token) for identifier in IDS):
                        # Prefixes are output-limit truncations, not typos.
                        truncations[(token, target, distance)] += 1
                    else:
                        wrong[(token, target, distance)] += 1
                        response_has_typo = True

            typo_responses += response_has_typo

        for future in futures[4:]:
            try:
                future.result()
            except Exception:
                pass

print(
    f"MODEL={MODEL} TEMP={TEMP} rounds={ROUNDS} "
    f"responses={responses} errors={errors} "
    f"errtypes={dict(error_types)} "
    f"elapsed={time.time() - started:.1f}s"
)

print(
    f"grounded_ids={grounded} exact={exact} "
    f"true_typos={sum(wrong.values())} "
    f"typo_responses={typo_responses} "
    f"rate={(sum(wrong.values()) / grounded if grounded else 0):.4%} "
    f"truncations={sum(truncations.values())}"
)

print("typo_forms:", dict(wrong.most_common(20)) or "NONE")

A true typo is a token with Levenshtein distance 1–2 from a canonical identifier that is not a prefix of one. Prefixes are counted separately as output-limit truncations.

3. Run the reproduction at temperature 0

TEST_MODEL=<served-model-name> \
TEST_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:30000 \
TEST_TEMP=0 \
TEST_ROUNDS=30 \
python3 -u dspark_typo_repro.py

4. Repeat at temperature 1

TEST_MODEL=<served-model-name> \
TEST_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:30000 \
TEST_TEMP=1 \
TEST_ROUNDS=30 \
python3 -u dspark_typo_repro.py

5. Run the non-speculative control

Relaunch the server with all --speculative-* flags removed while leaving every other launch argument unchanged. Repeat both commands above. This control produced zero true typos.

6. Test the block-size workaround

Relaunch DSPARK with a block size of 1: 

python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path <deepseek-v4-flash-0731> \
  --tp 4 \
  --attention-backend dsv4 \
  --moe-runner-backend marlin \
  --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \
  --speculative-dspark-block-size 1 \
  --max-running-requests 16 \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 16

Repeat the temperature-0 and temperature-1 tests. This configuration also produced zero true typos.

Expected result

At temperature 0, DSPARK should produce the same greedy token sequence as non-speculative decoding. All identifiers supplied verbatim in the prompt should be emitted without modification.

Observed result

With --speculative-dspark-block-size 6, the output silently contains plausible single-character corruptions such as: 

kimi-k3   -> kimi-kw
nova-x7   -> nova-7
apollo-n9 -> apollo-n11
wq-7f2b   -> wq-7f2e

In one temperature-0 run, 23 of 2,224 grounded identifiers were corrupted (1.0342%), affecting 15 of 120 target responses. The same test produced zero corruptions with speculative decoding disabled and with DSPARK block size 1.

Reproduction note

Changing --speculative-dspark-block-size changes num_tokens_per_req and may invalidate the DeepGEMM JIT shape cache. The first launch after changing the block size can require a long recompilation warmup. Allow enough startup time to prevent the server from being killed before it becomes ready.

### Environment Run this **inside the same Python environment/container used to launch the affected SGLang server**: ```bash python3 -m sglang.check_env 2>&1 | tee sglang_check_env.txt ``` Then paste the **complete command output verbatim** into that field, preferably wrapped as: ```text ``` Do not substitute the manually listed environment details; the maintainers explicitly require the actual `check_env` output.
